g.text: SUPERSEDED. Seeds 45 and 46 landed afterwards in ~/e0_run/d1_seeds4546/ and are included above; the stable arm's floor is 1.18x, not 1.003x.

text.style: font-size: 6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #5a5a5a

g.text: F3. Statistic R3 - the in-run tripwire statistic, NOT R1 - and the block is a TRAINING batch at global step 200, not a held-out set. The states behind these numbers were never

text.style: font-size: 6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #5a5a5a

g.text: saved, so they are [NOT RECOMPUTABLE] under R1, and no number in this figure may share an axis with any R1 value in this paper. The key is `train_rank_tripwire_observed` with

text.style: font-size: 6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #5a5a5a

g.text: the `train_` prefix, because querying it without the prefix returns [] and an empty list reads as a confident negative. The two rows are not connected and share only the axis:

text.style: font-size: 6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #5a5a5a

g.text: they are two arms, not a series. The reading is that rank's reproducibility is worst exactly where the arm is interesting - which is the configuration a practitioner is

text.style: font-size: 6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #5a5a5a

g.text: looking at when they reach for rank. F3 and F4(a) are not in conflict: F4(a) holds the model fixed and varies the patient sample; F3 holds the step fixed and varies the seed.
